name: Recital Q – 3
title: REPORT on EU-Syria political relations
part_text: Q. whereas the EU stood with the Syrian people throughout the war, including by fundraising and coordinating donor support through the Brussels conferences; whereas the EU continues to play this role through the Syria Partnership Coordination Forum, co-chaired by the EU and the Syrian transitional authorities and launched on 17 November 2026 in Damascus; whereas the EU remains one of the largest donors addressing the humanitarian and recovery needs arising from the Syrian crisis; whereas, since 2011, the EU and its Member States have collectively mobilised over EUR 41 billion in humanitarian, development, economic and stabilisation support for the Syrian people, making them the single largest international donor to the Syrian crisis; whereas at the ninth Brussels Conference on ‘Standing with Syria: meeting the needs for a successful transition’, held on 17 March 2025, the EU and its partners pledged approximately EUR 5.8 billion for Syria and the region for 2025 and 2026, of which nearly EUR 2.5 billion was pledged by the EU to support socio-economic recovery, reconstruction and humanitarian assistance; whereas in May 2025, the EU increased its humanitarian response for the region by allocating an additional EUR 20 million in humanitarian aid, specifically noting the precarious conditions in northeastern Syria;
